# Brief 1: logistics dashboard

**Composite. Not a real client.** Practice brief. Read it, do not edit it.

**Posted:** marketplace listing, fixed price
**Budget:** $1,200
**Timeline:** "ASAP, ideally 2 weeks"

---

Looking for a UI/UX designer to redesign the main dashboard of our logistics platform.

We are a small team building software for freight forwarders. Our users are operations staff who live in this tool for 8 hours a day. The current dashboard was built by our developers and it works, but it looks dated and customers mention it in sales calls.

**What we need:**

- Redesign of the main dashboard screen
- Modern, clean, professional look
- Must work with our existing component library (Material UI)
- Figma file with components

**Users:** operations coordinators at freight companies. Mostly 30 to 55. They are not designers and they do not want anything "fancy", but our newer competitors look much better than us and it is starting to hurt.

**Important:** the data density cannot be reduced. We tried a cleaner version last year and users hated it because they lost information they needed. Whatever you do, they still need to see everything they see now.

We have Google Analytics but honestly nobody looks at it much. Happy to introduce you to two customers for a call if that helps.

Let me know your availability and portfolio.

---

## Notes for the student

Do not read these until you have run the class exercise on the brief above.

<details>
<summary>What is actually going on here (open after you try)</summary>

- **"Modern and clean" plus "cannot reduce data density" is the contradiction**, and it is the whole job. Every instinct that makes a marketing page look clean, white space and generous padding and fewer elements, is unavailable. This is a hierarchy and typography problem, not a decluttering problem.
- **The real user is a power user.** Eight hours a day means they navigate by muscle memory. Moving something to make it prettier costs them speed and they will hate you for it. Ask what they do most often, not what looks worst.
- **Material UI is a locked constraint.** Ignore it and your file cannot be built.
- **The offer of two customer calls is the most valuable line in the brief** and most bidders will not take it.
- **The scope trap:** "the main dashboard screen" sounds like one screen. A dashboard has empty states, loading states, error states, filter states and at least two breakpoints. $1,200 for two weeks is fine for one screen and its states; it is a loss if "dashboard" quietly means the whole app.
- **What is missing entirely:** what the users actually do first thing in the morning. Nothing in this brief tells you the primary task.
</details>
